theme: Gig-economy and platform-economy datasets (Uber/DoorDash/Etsy/Upwork public data) used as cross-platform consumer-behaviour reads
queries_run: gh search repos "uber trip data dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "gig economy dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "uber movement data" --sort stars
gh search repos "app store ranking history" --sort stars
gh search repos "instacart market basket dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "freelance marketplace dataset upwork fiverr" --sort stars

candidates.name: PianoCrocodile/UberMovementData
candidates.what_it_holds: Automation script that downloaded daily cross-sectional Uber travel-time datasets from the Uber Movement website plus a cleaner/merger that reconstructs a time series from the aggregated averages; example range shown is Jan-Mar 2020. Uber discontinued the Uber Movement public site in April 2023, so this pull method is now dead against the live source, though it documents the schema for anyone who already has a Movement export.
candidates.why_useful: Would have been a rideshare/city-mobility volume proxy (gap 10, transport capacity) if still live; now only useful as a schema/parsing reference for any archived Uber Movement CSV exports someone already holds.
candidates.geography: Any city Uber Movement covered (variable by city, mostly US/major metros)
candidates.size_hint: Not stated; depends on city/date range pulled

candidates.name: RUCILab/Uber-Movement-Data-Scraping
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts for scraping data via the Uber Movement Data Toolkit for academic (RUCI Lab) research; no data files committed, method only.
candidates.why_useful: Same Uber Movement mobility angle as above; academic-grade scraper structure could guide re-implementation against any surviving archived Movement mirrors (e.g. Wayback captures).

candidates.name: alex-drake/ubermovements
candidates.what_it_holds: Joins Uber Movement travel-time exports with OpenStreetMap geometry; a processing pipeline rather than a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: same discontinued-source caveat, only useful if a raw Movement export is sourced elsewhere first.

candidates.name: alexrod61/doordash-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Single committed CSV (`doordash.csv`), a sample of DoorDash's own historical ETA-prediction dataset (order-level features: store/market id, item counts, order value, created-at/actual-delivery timestamps), originally released by DoorDash for a takehome/Kaggle exercise. Static, one vintage, no ongoing pull.
candidates.why_useful: Order-level delivery-app data is the closest committed 'gig/platform consumer behaviour' dataset found in this sweep; could sanity-check discretionary local-spend timing patterns (order value by day-of-week/hour) as a loose cross-platform consumer-strength read, but it is a fixed historical snapshot, not a refreshable time series, so it cannot feed a quarterly forecast on its own.
candidates.time_coverage: Single historical window (exact dates not documented in README)
candidates.size_hint: One CSV, row count unspecified (parent Kaggle DoorDash ETA dataset is ~197k rows)

candidates.name: dklim-git/DoorDash-Project
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-cleaning/visualization project built on the same DoorDash ETA sample dataset; likely re-hosts the CSV plus notebooks.
candidates.why_useful: Redundant with alexrod61/doordash-dataset; flagged only in case this copy has extra fields or a longer sample.

candidates.name: bright-cn/Etsy-dataset-sample
candidates.what_it_holds: 1,001-row sample of Etsy product listings (price, category, likely seller/shop fields) extracted via the Bright Data scraping API; mirrored identically across bright-kr, bright-jp, bright-data-de, luminati-io orgs (same content, different language READMEs).
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a working commercial scraping method for marketplace listing/pricing data (Etsy as a discretionary small-ticket consumer-spend proxy); the committed sample itself is too small (1,001 rows, single pull, no dates) to be a time series, so only the method is worth noting.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/fiverr
candidates.what_it_holds: A written third-party profile/description of Fiverr's public API surface (no data files, no committed dataset, no working scraper) — part of a large 'API Evangelist' series profiling gig/marketplace companies (also found: taskrabbit, instawork, helpling, zego, work-market, syft, shiftsmart, zolvers, zehitomo, stride-health, and dozens more under the gig-economy topic).
candidates.why_useful: Marginal at best: no data or method, just descriptive text about each platform's API. Listed only because the series maps which gig platforms expose any public API surface at all, which could point a future scout toward an actual client/SDK repo if one exists for a given platform.

notes: This theme has almost no committed-data footprint on GitHub search: gh search repos for 'gig economy dataset', 'app store ranking history', and 'freelance marketplace dataset upwork fiverr' returned zero hits, and 'etsy dataset' / 'uber movement data' / 'doordash dataset' / 'instacart market basket dataset' surfaced overwhelmingly single-well-known-static-dataset tutorial reruns (Instacart 2017 Kaggle basket data, one-time Etsy/DoorDash scrape samples) rather than anything time-series or refreshable -- excluded per the exclusion rule where they added nothing beyond re-analysis of one static file. Uber Movement (the one genuinely relevant mobility-as-consumer-behaviour source) was discontinued by Uber in April 2023, so every scraper/mirror repo found for it is now a dead pull against a retired site; kept at low potential as schema/method references only, not as live data. The 'topic:gig-economy' GitHub topic is dominated by API-Evangelist's auto-generated company-profile stubs (text descriptions, zero data) and new marketplace-app side-projects (HireBuddy, KasiLink, SevaSetu-Connect, Bounty, waggle) with no historical data of any kind -- these were excluded entirely as 'no data, no method'. WebSearch was unavailable for this scout (session web-search budget already exhausted before this task started), which limited verification to gh search plus WebFetch on raw READMEs/GitHub pages only; a re-run with WebSearch available would likely find more on Similarweb-style traffic-rank mirrors, Sensor Tower/App Annie rank-history scrapers, and BLS/CPS gig-worker survey microdata repos, none of which surfaced via gh search alone. Recommend a future scout try `gh search repos` for 'similarweb rank dataset', 'sensortower app rank', 'CPS contingent worker survey', and 'sherlock uber lyft fare data' once the search-API budget for this run resets.
